subject: Request for penetration test report — access and scope
messages:
From: Jake Ross <jake.ross@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_acct@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request for penetration test report — full copy

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team is reviewing Redwood for a pilot and they asked for a copy of your latest penetration test report (scope, findings, and remediation evidence). Could you share the full report or point us to where we can get it?

They specifically want:
- Full test report (vendor deliverable)
- Scope and methodology
- Evidence of remediation for high/critical items (screenshots, PRs, tickets)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement window is tight.

Jake Ross
Security Program Manager
Acme HealthTech

---
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Ross <jake.ross@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report — full copy

Hi Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. We absolutely understand where Acme is coming from. For third-party penetration test reports we have a controlled sharing policy: we do not distribute full vendor deliverables externally because they contain exploit details and attacker-oriented steps that increase risk if broadly circulated.

What we can offer immediately:
- An executive summary PDF that includes scope, a high-level findings list (no exploit chains), risk ratings, and remediation status. (Attached on the controlled share once NDA/ROE are agreed.)
- A CSV RAG (red/amber/green) of remediation items with current status and expected completion window.
- A live, on-screen review with your security team where we walk through the vendor report under an agreed Rules of Engagement (ROE). During that session we will not provide the raw exploit PoCs in downloadable form.

For Acme to access any non-public artifact we need either an existing MSA with an approved confidentiality exhibit or a short mutual NDA + an ROE signed by both parties. Neha (cc) from Legal can help accelerate the paperwork. Marissa (cc) is our SE and can schedule the on-screen review and share the summary artifacts once NDA/ROE are in place.

To move forward today I can: send the executive summary and RAG as a controlled Drive link (view-only) and propose times for a 45-minute technical review next week. Which do you prefer?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: (we will provide view-only links post-NDA)
- PT_Summary_2026-06.pdf (executive summary)
- Remediation_RAG_2026-06.csv (status table)
From: Jake Ross <jake.ross@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_acct@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for penetration test report — full copy

Hannah —

Thanks for the quick reply and for outlining the process. A few clarifying items from our side before we start paperwork:
1) Our risk team will need confirmation that there were no unremediated critical findings in the last cycle, or if there were, the mitigation compensating controls.
2) For the RAG, can you indicate which findings were found in customer-facing APIs vs. internal infra?
3) For remediation evidence, screenshots of the fix in staging + the linked ticket/PR are ideal. Is that something we can get in the controlled share?

We'd prefer to do the on-screen review first before signing an NDA if possible — driven by internal policy that limits external document ingestion. Is Redwood willing to host a recorded, view-only session where your SE walks through the vendor report (muted/obscured exploit details) while our engineers observe? If so, propose slots for next Tue/Wed.

Jake

Jake —

Appreciate the context and the timeline. We can accommodate the on-screen, recorded review under the following conditions (standard for all customers):
- Attendees must be named and listed in an ROE (no open links).
- Recording is permitted but the recording will be retained by Redwood and shared only if mutually agreed; the raw vendor artifact will not be included.
- We will obscure or omit exploit PoCs and any step-by-step attack chains from the visible slides.

Regarding your three asks:
1) Critical findings: our latest pen test (May 2026) had 1 critical finding that was mitigated in staging and closed in prod on 2026-05-22. The executive summary includes the timeline and mitigation approach.
2) Findings classification: the summary and the RAG include a column 'surface' with values (public API / internal infra / admin console). We can highlight the customer-facing items during the walkthrough.
3) Remediation evidence: yes — screenshots from staging with PR/ticket links will be available in the controlled share after the ROE is executed. For privacy we will redact internal IPs and any customer-identifying data.

Proposed slots for the on-screen review (PT walkthrough, 45 minutes):
- Tue 2026-06-16 09:00–09:45 PT
- Tue 2026-06-16 13:00–13:45 PT
- Wed 2026-06-17 10:00–10:45 PT

If any of those work, reply with the attendee list and we'll send an ROE and a view-only drive link to the executive summary and RAG.

Attaching controlled artifacts (view-only):
- PT_Summary_2026-06.pdf
- Remediation_RAG_2026-06.csv

Thanks — looking forward to the review.
